step: RECURRENCE ESCALATION (runbook mandatory rule, plan section 3)
goal: auto:GluedIdentifierValidator has OPEN heal tickets from 2 distinct source pages (content/blog.aspose.org/pdf/python/pdf-generated-in-python/index.md and content/docs.aspose.org/en/cells/rust/getting-started/quickstart.md) with no Track-B taskcard ever implemented for it -- decide whether a real producer-side fix exists before opening any new Track-A page, per the runbook's closed-loop requirement.

assumptions.assumption: The 13 entries in wave-pdfgeneratedpython-20260911's final summary.json failed_shard_ids (nl,pl,pt,ro,ru,sv,th,tr,uk,vi,zh plus es,fa) are all real exhausted-retry failures.
assumptions.evidence: failure_metadata.jsonl for that campaign_id has only 9 rows, covering es/fa/hi/it -- not the other 9 languages. Cross-checked against disk (only the 12 accepted locale files exist) and against heal_queue.jsonl: nl/pl/pt/ro/ru/sv/th/tr/uk/vi/zh each carry two auto:unclassified tickets with an EMPTY note field, which _append_heal_ticket() in campaign_runner.py only produces when self.ledger.latest_failure() finds no failure record at all for that (output_path, target_lang) -- i.e. the cell was never attempted. Root cause: heal_queue.py's QU-02 per-file quarantine (is_source_path_quarantined, PER_FILE_QUARANTINE_THRESHOLD=3) tripped mid-run once a 3rd distinct locale (de, from this session's own m2m100 retry campaign running concurrently) got an OPEN auto:GluedIdentifierValidator ticket for this exact source_path, on top of the 2 the main campaign had already opened for es/fa. Every subsequent locale in the main campaign's manifest was then skipped via the same _append_heal_ticket() call path (campaign_runner.py:2185-2192) without ever being attempted. This is QU-02 working as designed, not a crash; the peer session that closed the page at 12/25 read the misleading 'failed_shard_ids' label and did not distinguish attempted-and-exhausted from never-attempted.

assumptions.assumption: GluedIdentifierValidator failures on the description frontmatter field are pure model stochasticity with no producer-side fix available (the validator's own docstring's stated conclusion for its 'generation-time' path).
assumptions.evidence: Read text_unit_extractor.py's _extract_frontmatter_units (line 819): frontmatter string fields DO get placeholder_manager.protect(field_value, self.preserve_patterns) applied, using the SAME global body.preserve_patterns list as body text (confirmed by the TC-APT-103 comment in config/global.yaml itself describing a prior incident that also manifested 'via the frontmatter summary field'). Neither of the two existing patterns (backtick code-span, bare PascalCase compound) matches this page's actual identifiers: the description field's 'aspose_pdf.generated' and 'aspose_pdf' are lower_snake_case with a dot, appearing with no backticks (frontmatter strings carry no markdown code-span syntax). So these specific identifiers were reaching the model as fully unprotected plain prose, not merely 'sometimes glued by a protected placeholder's restore step' -- a real, closeable gap distinct from the validator docstring's already-accepted pure-dot 'Workbook.save'-style stochastic case. Two live debug_translate_one.py reverification attempts (es and fa, professionalize_llm, fresh generations, not TM-cached) after locating this gap both came back clean (no GluedIdentifierValidator issue) -- consistent with the failure being real but genuinely intermittent per-attempt even for the unprotected shape, so this fix reduces exposure rather than deterministically guaranteeing zero recurrence; the residual model-stochasticity risk on the (rarer) pure-dot identifier shape remains gate-only-catchable, exactly as the validator's docstring already documents for that separate shape.

two_approaches_considered.approach: Do nothing new: treat this as pre-accepted model stochasticity (per the validator's own docstring) and MODEL_LIMITATION_DEFERRED the 3 tickets (es, fa, de) without a code change.
two_approaches_considered.rejected_because: The docstring's 'no extractor-side fix can close the class alone' conclusion was reached for the general glued-identifier class across both its documented mechanisms; it was not re-examined for the specific sub-case of a bare, non-backtick, snake_case/dotted identifier appearing in a FRONTMATTER STRING field, which has a concrete, unprotected gap (no preserve_pattern reaches it) distinct from the body-text 'Workbook.save' pure-dot example the docstring evidences. Deferring without closing the concrete gap would leave the SAME preventable exposure live for every other page whose description/summary/title mentions a snake_case module or file name -- already true for the docs.aspose.org/rust quickstart page's independent occurrence of this class.

two_approaches_considered.approach: (chosen) Add a third body.preserve_patterns entry that placeholder-protects bare snake_case/dotted identifiers requiring at least one underscore segment, mirroring the existing backtick and PascalCase entries; keep the pure-dot shape ('Workbook.save') explicitly out of scope since that remains genuinely gate-only-catchable per the docstring's own evidence.
two_approaches_considered.why_chosen: Closes the concrete, verified gap (frontmatter fields reaching the model with zero protection for this identifier shape) using the SAME mechanism and file already used for two prior instances of this exact defect family (TC-ICR-003 backtick patterns, TC-APT-103 PascalCase pattern) -- consistent precedent, not a novel mechanism. Underscore-gating (not dot-gating) is the key design choice: no natural-language prose in any of the 25 portfolio languages uses an underscore, so this cannot false-positive on ordinary Latin abbreviations ('e.g.', 'i.e.', 'U.S.') the way a dot-only pattern would; verified with a dedicated regression suite (tests/regression/test_snake_case_dotted_identifier_protection.py, 8 tests) plus the full existing preserve_patterns suite (44 tests total, all green) after fixing one real regression the new pattern caused (it matched PlaceholderManager's own reserved '{PLACEHOLDER_N}' token during protect()'s sequential multi-pattern cascade, double-wrapping it -- fixed with a `(?!PLACEHOLDER_)` negative lookahead).

expected_outcome_falsifiable: With the new preserve_pattern live, a fresh debug_translate_one.py run of pdf-generated-in-python's description field for any target language will show 'aspose_pdf.generated'/'aspose_pdf' substituted with a {PLACEHOLDER_N} token before the model call (verifiable via TextUnitExtractor unit tests, already passing) and the GluedIdentifierValidator issue rate for this specific (source_path, field=description) pair should measurably drop across a re-run of the full remaining locale set -- it is not expected to reach exactly zero, since the validator's other detection paths (restore-time space-dropping on an intact placeholder, and any other unprotected identifier shape) remain live and gate-catchable by design.
regression_control: tests/regression/test_snake_case_dotted_identifier_protection.py (8 tests: 4 positive protection cases including the exact failing fragment, 4 negative false-positive-avoidance cases including Latin abbreviations, version numbers, and the explicitly-out-of-scope pure-dot shape) plus the pre-existing tests/regression/test_pascal_compound_identifier_protection.py (12 tests) and tests/unit/translation_engine/test_ast_frontmatter_preserve_pattern_parity.py -- all 44 tests pass after the PLACEHOLDER-collision fix.
disposition: Implemented config/global.yaml body.preserve_patterns addition + regression tests. Retriggering pdf-generated-in-python's remaining/quarantined cells (es, fa, de, nl, pl, pt, ro, ru, sv, th, tr, uk, vi, zh) under the hardened config next; the 3 real GluedIdentifierValidator tickets (es, fa, de) get their disposition updated once that retrigger's outcome is known, which will also clear the QU-02 file-level quarantine for this page (currently OPEN-ticket count for this (source_path, root_cause_class) pair is 3, at the threshold) since a resolved disposition no longer counts toward it. The 22 auto:unclassified tickets from never-attempted locales are left as-is (their OPEN status will naturally resolve once those locales are actually attempted and either accepted or newly ticketed by this retrigger) -- not touching them individually avoids a second wave of ticket-file churn for rows that were never a real defect signal in the first place.
